questions.note: Height and leg lengths read right, but the upper arms and deltoids are inflated like a padded suit, which with the wide pauldrons makes the head look small and the shoulders too broad. The figure reads as a game-asset blockout, not the lean man of the reference.

Stance, foot spread and the low diagonal carbine match. The outline breaks at the swollen upper arms, the flat slab pauldrons standing off the shoulder, and the oversized knee pads. Hair is a smooth cap with spikes at the crown, not the reference's textured crop.

Every item is roughly where the reference puts it: gaiter, carrier with three mag pouches, antenna, pauldrons, forearm guards, gloves, belt, leg rigs, knee pads, boots. But the knee pad caps are oversized cushions, the pauldrons are thin cards, and the elbow pad is a tiny puck stuck on the outside of the elbow.

Mostly stacked, but the shirt and trousers are shrink-wrapped to the body, so the back muscles and buttocks show through. The shoulder-strap tops end in torn, jagged polygons, the elbow sleeve steps in hard rings, and there is a straight material seam above each knee pad.

The clothing has no bulk: the sleeves and torso read as a wetsuit with no folds at the elbow or armpit. The arm volume comes from the body, not the cloth. Carrier and pouches are clean blocks with no fill or sag. The lower trouser legs carry an even, crumpled noise rather than blousing folds.

The right hand sits on the pistol grip with the index finger along the receiver, which reads as a real hold. The left hand drapes its fingers over the top of the handguard, and the three-quarter left view shows it open beside the handguard, palm up, not closed on it. Glove fingers are rubbery cylinders.

defects.what: Hair is a single smooth shell with a hard painted hairline and a few jagged polygon tufts at the crown. The clay views show the crown as scattered shards; there are no strands, no fade at the sides and no breakup at the edge.
defects.fix: A short crop has thousands of short strands, a soft fade into the skin at the temples and nape, and a broken outline against the background.

defects.what: The carrier shoulder-strap tops beside the gaiter end in torn, sawtooth polygon edges, as if the mesh were clipped or has tearing. The other side, at about x 850 to 1010, does the same.
defects.fix: Shoulder straps are continuous padded webbing with sewn, rounded ends that run over the shoulder to the back panel.

defects.what: The right pauldron reads as a thin flat card with a wavy, ragged outline and a raised rim. It is filled with a soft grey blotch noise that has no relation to its edges or form.
defects.fix: A moulded shoulder plate is domed with a crisp, even edge thickness. Wear concentrates on the edges and high points as scuffs and chips.

defects.what: The shirt sleeve is shrink-wrapped and featureless over an inflated upper arm: no folds at the armpit or elbow crook, and a uniform matte surface like neoprene.
defects.fix: A combat shirt sleeve has slack: it gathers under the armpit and in the elbow crook, and bags slightly between the armour bands.

defects.what: Above the left elbow the sleeve breaks in hard, stepped horizontal ridges, like two shells meeting. The clay full view shows the same rings at the elbow.
defects.fix: Cloth over a bent elbow forms soft compression folds on the inside and stretches smoothly over the point.

defects.what: The elbow pad is a small puck stuck to the outside of the elbow, apparently floating proud of the sleeve, with no strap visible holding it.
defects.fix: An elbow pad cups the point of the elbow, sits tight to the sleeve, and has a visible strap or sleeve.

defects.what: The left hand is open beside the handguard, palm up, with its fingers not wrapped round it. In the hero view the fingers only drape over the top of the rail.
defects.fix: A support hand closes round the handguard: thumb over the top or side, fingers wrapped underneath, the palm in contact.

defects.what: The trouser fabric shows a coarse linen-like grid at least five times too large for ripstop. The camo is soft foggy blobs floating over it, with no printed edge and no interaction with the weave.
defects.fix: Ripstop's grid is a few millimetres and barely visible at this distance. Printed camo has defined edges that break with the weave and fade at the wear points.

defects.what: Above each knee pad the trouser texture stops at a straight line and gives way to a flat, untextured black band. The same happens on the other leg at about x 1560 to 1900, y 30 to 110.
defects.fix: Trousers carry the same fabric into the knee-pad pocket. Any neoprene sleeve is tucked under the cloth, not showing as a clean band.

defects.what: The knee pad caps read as puffy cushions with a tan rim and a soft grey blotch fill. There is no hard-plastic sheen, the edges are not crisp, and the wear follows no logic.
defects.fix: A knee cap is a stiff moulded shell with defined facets and a sharp rim. Scuffing and dirt collect on the front face and edges.

defects.what: The right boot's forefoot is a smooth, flat-topped wedge like a rubber galosh. It has a uniform satin finish with no creasing at the flex line and no scuffs, stitching or panel edges.
defects.fix: A worn leather boot creases across the ball of the foot. The toe cap and panels are separated by stitched seams, and the leather shows scuffs and dust.

defects.what: The lower trouser legs carry an even, high-frequency crinkle over their whole surface, like crumpled foil. It reads as noise, not the few large blousing folds of trousers over boots.
defects.fix: Bloused trousers form a handful of large stacked folds above the boot top and hang smoothly above them.

defects.what: The laces are thin uniform wires in a perfectly regular X, floating above the tongue with no flattening, slack or shadow under them.
defects.fix: Laces are flat braided cord that bends over the eyelets, lies on the tongue, and varies in tension.

defects.what: The carbine is one flat, satin dark grey throughout, with razor-sharp edges, no edge wear, and no difference between the anodised receiver, the polymer furniture and the steel barrel.
defects.fix: A used M4 shows anodised aluminium wearing silver on the edges. The polymer furniture is matter, the barrel and muzzle device are a darker phosphate, and there is dust in the recesses.

defects.what: Where the shoulder strap meets the carrier, the buckle hardware stacks into a pile of folded, overlapping plates that seem to intersect each other.
defects.fix: A strap buckle is a single ladder-lock or cobra buckle with the webbing threaded through it.

defects.what: The carrier and its pouches are clean, flat-coloured blocks with no wear, edge darkening, stitching, fabric texture at this scale, or bulge from the magazines inside.
defects.fix: A used Cordura carrier has visible weave, faded high points, dirt in the seams, and pouches that bulge round the magazines.

defects.what: From behind, the shirt shows the back muscles and the trousers show the buttocks as if painted on. The cloth follows the anatomy exactly, with no slack or drape.
defects.fix: A combat shirt and trousers hang off the shoulder blades and the seat, bridging the hollows with a few drape folds.

defects.what: At the bottom of the right-thigh pouch hangs a thin, wire-like hook or loop that does not attach to anything readable.
defects.fix: Any lanyard or retention loop is visible webbing or cord, attached at both ends.

ranked: Overall the figure reads as a clean game-asset blockout. Every surface has the same even roughness, and nothing has the dirt, fading, seams or stitching the reference shows on every item.
[D4] [D17] The shirt and trousers are shrink-wrapped: sleeves like a wetsuit over bloated upper arms, back muscles and buttocks showing through. Real combat clothing has slack, gathers and drape.
[D1] The hair is a smooth shell with a hard hairline and polygon shards at the crown. A short crop needs strands, a fade at the temples and a broken outline.
The skin's orange waxy finish is declared, but it dominates the head view and hides whether the face form is right. Even so, the eye sockets read dark and dead and there is no stubble.
[D3] The pauldrons are thin cards with ragged outlines and a grey blotch noise. The forearm guards and knee caps carry the identical noise, so the same procedural pattern repeats on every plate.
[D7] The left hand does not close on the handguard: its fingers drape over the top in the hero view, and it is open beside it in the three-quarter left view.
[D2] The shoulder-strap tops by the gaiter end in torn, sawtooth polygons on both sides, which reads as mesh tearing.
[D8] The trouser weave is a coarse grid far too large for ripstop, and the camo is soft fog with no printed edges. Together they give the trousers a projected-texture look.
[D10] The knee caps are puffy cushions with a tan rim, not stiff moulded shells, and are larger than the reference's.
[D11] The right boot's toe is a smooth wedge like a galosh, with uniform satin leather: no flex creases, toe cap seam or scuffs.
[D14] The carbine is a single satin grey with razor edges. It has no anodised wear, no polymer and steel contrast and no dust, so the most-looked-at prop reads most like CG.
[D16] The carrier and pouches are flat blocks without weave, wear or magazine bulge. The front panel's dark rectangles read as boolean cuts.
[D9] Above each knee pad there is a straight seam where the trouser texture stops and gives way to a plain black band.
[D5] The left elbow sleeve steps in hard horizontal ridges where it should fold softly.
[D12] The lower trouser legs carry an even, crumpled noise instead of a few large blousing folds.
Gloves: the fingers are smooth rubbery cylinders and the knuckle pads are blocky, with no stitching or seam lines. The cuff merges into the sleeve with no edge.
[D6] The elbow pad is a tiny puck stuck on the outside of the elbow, visibly proud of the sleeve.
[D15] The buckle hardware where the strap meets the carrier piles into intersecting folded plates.
[D13] The laces are uniform wires in a perfect X, floating above the tongue.
[D18] A thin hook dangles from the bottom of the right-thigh pouch, attached to nothing readable.
The light is consistent across the views and with the shadows, but the contact shadows under the boots are weak, so the feet sit lightly on the floor.
